claim: For every integer \(T\ge2\), let \(N(T)\) count distinct nondegenerate Lucas sequences \(U_0=0,\ U_1=1,\ U_{n+2}=AU_{n+1}-BU_n\), with \(A,B\in\mathbb Z\) and both roots of \(x^2-Ax+B\) in \(|z|\le T\). Then \(N(T)=4T^3-2T^2-2T-2\lfloor T/\sqrt2\rfloor-2\lfloor T/\sqrt3\rfloor\).

correctness.rationale: The root-bound criterion is proved in both directions. The integer-point count is exact, the \(AB=0\) union is counted once at the intersection, and all possible root-of-unity orders in a quadratic field are classified. The repeated-root family is included separately. The resulting subtraction gives the stated formula for every integer \(T\ge2\).

value.rationale: The number of integer Lucas recurrences under a root-modulus bound is a natural parameter-counting invariant. The exact formula resolves the count at every integer radius, improving the previously published two-sided bounds for this same object and making the contribution of the repeated-root and cyclotomic degeneracies explicit.
